newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish budget will show surplus in 1998 - PM.
newsitem.headline: Swedish budget will show surplus in 1998 - PM.

text.p: Sweden's budget will show a surplus in 1998, which could be used for health care, elderly care and education, Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Wednesday.
"Public finances are developing much better than we thought," Persson said during a debate in parliament between party leaders.

"For 1998, we will have a balanced budget, but we will also have some room on top of that. There will be a surplus of about 10 billion crowns ($1.4 billion), which will be used to strengthen health care, care for the elderly and children and schools."
The government has said it will have a balanced budget in 1998 and that an expected 1999 budget surplus will be used to pay off state debt.
The 1999 surplus will, as previously announced, be used to pay off state debt, Persson told journalists after the debate.
"First, after 1998, (we) will start paying off state debt. The year 1999 will be a time of surpluses. That does not exclude that there will be a crown left also in 1998."
-- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019 ($ = 7.133 Swedish Crowns)
